task.title: Tilt elements in three dimensions
task.shortdesc: With three-dimensional transforms you tilt an element as if it were a sheet of paper in space, and with a perspective you make the near edge larger than the far one.

info.p: The drawing is a plane with the x axis to the right, the y axis down and the z axis pointing to the reader. The functions of transform that work in space are:

row.entry: Turn the element around one of the axes. rotateZ() is rotate().
Turns the element around the axis that goes from the origin to the point x, y, z. The numbers can have any size, because only the direction counts. When all three are 0, the element does not turn.
Move the element, in the third dimension too.
Scale the element, in the third dimension too.

Makes what is closer to the reader larger and what is farther smaller. The length is the distance from the reader to the drawing. A length below 1 pixel counts as 1 pixel, and none gives no perspective.
Gives the sixteen numbers of the transform, column by column.

info.p: The properties rotate, translate and scale also take three dimensions, as Move, turn and scale elements shows.
Without a perspective, the drawing is projected straight onto the page. A turn around the x or y axis then only makes the element narrower, and a movement along z changes nothing you can see.

You can add a perspective in two ways. The function perspective() at the start of a transform list works for that element only. The property perspective on a group works for the children of the group, and they all share the same point of view. The group itself is not changed by its own perspective.

A smaller distance gives a stronger effect. The perspective-origin property sets the point of view, the place where the reader looks from, on the plane of the drawing. Its initial value is 50% 50%, the center of the reference box of the group. It takes the same values as background-position: lengths, percentages and the keywords left, center, right, top and bottom.

fig.title: A rotation without a perspective, with one in the transform and with one on the parent

image.alt: Three rectangles with a dashed outline mark the starting places. The first is turned around its vertical axis and looks narrower. The second and the third also turn, and the edge nearer to the reader is taller than the farther one.

step.cmd: Put several elements in the same space

info.p: Each element with a three-dimensional transform is a plane. By default the children of a group are flattened into the plane of the group, so two planes that cross each other are drawn one after the other, in the order of the document. With transform-style: preserve-3d on the group, its children keep their own planes in one shared space. CSSMedia cuts the planes where they cross and draws the parts from the farthest to the nearest.

Some properties make the group flat even if you ask for preserve-3d: an overflow that is not visible or clip, an opacity below 1, a clip-path, a mask, an isolation of isolate and a mix-blend-mode other than normal.

step.cmd: Hide the back of an element

info.p: When you turn an element so far that you see its back, CSSMedia draws it, as a mirror image. With backface-visibility: hidden it draws nothing while the back faces the reader. The initial value is visible.
A clipPath, a gradient and a pattern are always flat. CSSMedia ignores the three-dimensional functions of their transforms and applies the flat ones.
